# v1 alpha: session launch prompts

Local only. Plan: `.claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md`. Open each session in `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto`, set model and effort, paste the prompt. Sessions run unattended; they come back to you only to merge.

| Session | Work | `/model` | `/effort` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Release model | F1 -> F2 -> G -> H -> M | Opus 5.5 | medium |
| 2 Publish chain | D -> L -> J | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 3 Fixes | A, B, C (workflow), then K (after G merges) and N | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 5 Identity and graph | E -> I | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 4 Evidence (after E and F2 merge) | Q | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |

Opus spend is limited to Session 1 (one cross-cutting semantic change, where a rework loop costs more than Opus) and to subagents: an Opus design note at the start of L, E and Q, and the Opus reviewer per PR.

Capacity: disk is the limit (about 98 GB free; stale worktree `target/` dirs hold about 89 GB, all regenerable). With debug info off, expect a few GB per active worktree. Sessions 1, 3 (three Wave 0 worktrees) and 5 build at once from the start; Session 2 starts with them because J's first change is tiny, and its heavier builds overlap Wave 0 finishing.

Before launch, free the stale build output (build artifacts only, no source or branches touched):

```
cd ~/Projects/callisto && rm -rf .claude/worktrees/*/target
```

Launch all from a shell in the repo (each prints an id; `claude agents` lists them, `claude attach <id>` watches one):

```
cd ~/Projects/callisto
claude --bg --model opus   --effort medium "Run Session 1 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 2 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Use a workflow: run Session 3 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 5 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
# after E and F2 merge:
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 4 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
```

## Session 1

```
Implement work packages F1, F2, G, H, then M from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each, in order. Its root-cause table (R1, R6) and settled decisions are the spec. Trails: #457 for F1, F2, G, H; #458 for M. Link with `entire trail link`; do not create trails.
Done when: a pre cycle runs end to end through the release-PR flow (pre enter -> beta.0 -> fresh fix -> beta.1 -> nothing new -> no PR -> pre exit -> stable), inferred-only changes open a release PR, malformed-only changesets fail decide, and a Changesets v3 pre.json repo works mid-cycle.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 2

```
Implement work packages D, L, then J from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each, in order. Its root-cause table (R3, R7) and settled decisions are the spec. Trails: #357 for D; #459 for L and J. Link with `entire trail link`; do not create trails.
Done when: generated workflows carry any valid branch name exactly in both templates; no job that runs project code holds id-token or registry credentials; npm-family publishes a packed tarball with --ignore-scripts; twine and crates.io can publish with no token through native OIDC (unproven against real registries until I run it).
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 3

```
Use a workflow for work packages A, B and C from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md: one worktree and PR each, pipeline implement (sonnet) -> mutants -> fresh review (opus) -> gate, under 10 agents, cargo lock shared. Trail #357 for A, B, C.
Then K (after Session 1 merges G) and N, both on trail #458. Link with `entire trail link`; do not create trails.
Done when: policy recipes fail when cargo fails; the HTTP parser keeps a body with blank lines; JSON input errors carry their origin; a Changesets v2 or v3 config migrates with every ignored key reported; peer dependents get a patch by default.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 5

```
Implement work packages E, then I from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each. Its root-cause table (R2, R4) and settled decisions are the spec. Trail #357.
Done when: equivalent PyPI or crates.io names cannot both be admitted and two such owners produce zero provider effects; relative workspace: lookup is indexed, with before/after bench numbers.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 4 (after E and F2 merge)

```
Implement work package Q from .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md. Choose the narrowest test-only way past registry_endpoint.rs's https rule. Trail #460. Link with `entire trail link`; do not create trails.
Done when: `just verify-real` rehearses partial publish -> rerun adopts, delayed visibility, a conflicting tag and a missing Python artifact against local npm, cargo and PyPI registries through production registry binding, and exits nonzero on any wrong outcome.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules".
```

## Session 6 (QA swarm, Git boundary and plan binding)

```
Implement work packages S, T, then V from the "QA swarm 2026-11-18" section of .claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md, one PR each, in order, off fresh origin/main. Evidence: .claude/plans/qa-2026-11-18/report.md (read QA-01, QA-03, QA-04, QA-05). Trail #462.
Done when: recovery after an interruption refuses (never succeeds with) a plan from a differently named or space-prefixed sibling workspace, asserting final package identity, version, note consumption and changelog; a package directory ending in * gets only its own commits; a commit body with U+001E infers normally; a Cargo-only dependency orders only the Cargo output of a dual owner, and an npm-only one only the npm output. Owner-level cycle policy is unchanged.
Follow .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md "Rules". CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5 while five sessions build.
```

## Rules

- Before each WP: `git fetch`; re-verify the plan's finding against current main (other sessions merge in between). If another session already owns the WP's branch, skip to your next WP.
- Work in a named worktree per WP (EnterWorktree), branched off origin/main. No stacks. Each worktree builds into its own `target/`, so builds in different worktrees run in parallel with no lock; never run two builds in the same worktree.
- Build budget, exported once per session: `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` (debug info is most of each `target/`; dropping it cuts disk and link time), `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(( $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) / 4 ))` and the same value for nextest `--test-threads`, so four builders share the CPU.
- Mutation testing runs in place in the WP worktree after committing: `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <diff>`; it reuses the worktree's `target/` instead of copying the tree.
- Start independent pieces early in their own worktrees: Session 1 runs G's `pre.json` reader/writer (`model/format/pre.rs`) as a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` while it works on F1; Session 2 ships J's twine environment change (`runner.rs`) first. Only the parts that touch shared files wait for their chain.
- Start the reviewer subagent as soon as the diff is final, in parallel with the gate and mutation run; it reads, it never builds.
- When a WP's PR is open and green, `rm -rf <worktree>/target`; after merge, remove the worktree and its local branch.
- Fix the root cause by the first rung that works: type or private constructor, exhaustive match, existing lint, one test at the real boundary. Write that test first. Delete checks the type makes redundant. Fix siblings in the same PR.
- Specs, ADRs and docs/architecture change in the same PR as behaviour.
- Gate by exit code, unsandboxed in the worktree: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`, then `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP's Rust diff with zero missed (an equivalent mutant gets one line in the PR body).
- Design-heavy WPs (L, E, Q): first spawn one Opus subagent (general-purpose, model opus) with the plan's finding and root-cause row; it returns a short design (types, signatures, call sites to migrate, the boundary test). Implement against it yourself.
- One fresh-context reviewer per PR (general-purpose, model opus) given only the diff and the finding. Apply what holds up.
- Stay at the launched effort; do not escalate unless the same gate failure repeats.
- Ship without asking: signed commit, `callisto add` changeset for released-behaviour changes, push, `entire trail ci-pr`. No session links. Never merge.
- Ask me only when something requires me: a credential or account, or a plan claim that is false in a way that changes the design.

148-- Wave 0 (now, disjoint files): A, B, C.
149-- Wave 1: D, E, F1. E and F1 both touch `release_decision.rs` at different ranges: `git merge-tree` before the second merges.
150-- Wave 2 (critical path, serial): F2 -> G -> H. In parallel: I (after E, shares `walk.rs`), L (after D, shares templates and `init.rs`), N.
151-- Wave 3: J (after L), K (after G), M (after F2, shares `status.rs`), Q (after E and F2, so it rehearses the fixed model).
152-- Wave 4: R, then the external pilot.
153-
154-Critical path: F1 -> F2 -> G -> H. Second chain: D -> L -> J.

156-## How the swarm runs
157-
158-- One named worktree per WP, branch off `main`, no stacks; merge in wave order.
159-- Builds: each worktree has its own target dir; every cargo invocation takes one machine-wide lock (`flock $TMPDIR/callisto-cargo.lock cargo ...`), so agents overlap on thinking and editing, never on builds.
160-- Per WP: the implementer writes the regression first, driving the real binary or function at the boundary named in the finding, then the type change, then deletes checks the type now covers.
161-- Proof by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`; `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP diff with zero missed except argued equivalents (it found two real gaps on a caliper branch today); sibling sweep listed in the PR body.
162-- Review: one fresh-context Opus reviewer per WP, given the diff and the finding, not the implementer's reasoning.
163-- Gates run unsandboxed in the worktree: sandboxed runs fail tests that write inside the repo and look like defects.
164-- Ship: signed commit, changeset via `callisto add`, push, link the WP's trail, never create one: #357 Callisto fails predictably (A-E, I); #457 Managed prerelease and inferred release PRs (F1, F2, G, H); #458 Changesets v2 and v3 users can switch (K, M, N); #459 Publish isolation and trusted publishing (L, J); #460 Release recovery evidence (Q, R).
165-- Orchestration: a Workflow script can run each wave as a pipeline (implement -> mutate -> review -> gate), with the build lock as the only shared resource; it needs an explicit "use a workflow".

168-
169-GitHub-hosted, Linux/macOS, Cargo + npm (napi-rs included), separate-directory Python. Out: Windows, other forges, co-located Maturin, private/HTML PyPI, staged npm publish.

172-
173-Decided; sessions do not ask.
174-
175-1. ADR 2's consequence bullet amended: inferred-only release PRs allowed through `release-trigger`.
176-2. Decision schema v3 with `consumed_changesets`; readers accept 1-3.
177-3. `pre.json` written back in the shape read.
178-4. Cargo `foo-bar`/`foo_bar` in one workspace is E100.
179-5. `init --workflow` adds the workflow when `callisto.toml` exists.
180-6. OIDC before 1.0, after R7, with `id-token: write` on this repo's `execute` job.
181-7. Peer default moves to v3's patch policy, shipped as Breaking.
182-8. One changed-without-changeset flag on `status`.
183-9. Builds run in parallel across worktrees (each has its own `target/`); never two in one worktree. WP A rewords AGENTS.md's "Never run cargo builds in parallel" to say "in the same checkout".
184-

186-
187-- Launching the sessions.
188-- Merging PRs (sessions never merge), in wave order.
189-- Registry accounts for R (tokenless publish, onboarding time) and the external pilot.

Six new confirmed defects: **one high, four medium and one low**, including one confirmed performance defect. Every finding has an independent validation pass. Final correctness reproductions use a newly built binary from frozen revision `fac8cadf91f792fdd17dec93d36eeb10be24e5f3`.

The live checkout advanced from `ab3c030` while discovery ran. I preserved those external merges, archived the newer source into `source-fac8cadf91/`, built it in `current-build/`, and repeated the findings against that binary. Initial discovery and some exploratory optimized benchmarks used the older binary; they are explicitly distinguished below. No implementation changes, commits, pushes or registry/forge effects were made by this audit. All audit artifacts remain outside the public repository.

**Complete new finding list**

| ID | Severity | Finding | Current source anchor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| QA-01 | High | Interrupted version recovery can apply a sibling workspace's plan | [checkpoint.rs:198](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/checkpoint.rs:198) |
| QA-02 | Medium | Python requirement rewrites drop epochs and weaken constraints | [python.rs:823](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:823) |
| QA-03 | Medium | Terminal `*` in a package directory selects sibling commits | [access.rs:700](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:700) |
| QA-04 | Low | A valid record-separator character in a commit body stops inference | [access.rs:907](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:907) |
| QA-05 | Medium | Publication dependencies leak across an owner's native outputs | [derive.rs:503](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:503) |
| QA-06 | Medium | Historical ownership checks repeat Git probes for the same commit | [tags.rs:259](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:259) |

Source links point into the live checkout and can move. The immutable inspected copies are under `source-fac8cadf91/` alongside this report.

**QA-01 — Recovery can successfully apply the wrong workspace plan. CONFIRMED.**

An independent fixture contains sibling directories `  release-work` and `release-work`. The first owns `primary-package`3.4.5 with a patch changeset; the second owns `other-package`3.4.5 with a minor changeset. An ordinary dry run correctly proposes primary3.4.6. The test interrupts the real CLI immediately after successful checkpoint creation, before version writes, then retries.

The retry exits0 but reports other-package3.5.0, writes3.5.0 into the primary manifest, consumes the primary patch note, and writes a primary-directory changelog headed `other-package` with the sibling's minor note. The actual sibling remains unchanged. Root reproduced this again on the frozen current binary; `recovery-current/independent-results.json` and `replay.log` contain the before/interruption/after sequence.

The first loss is `git_stdout_env` using `stdout_trimmed` for a path. Both the recorded and current workspace prefix lose their leading spaces, so their equality check still passes. `open_checkpoint_tree` then opens the trimmed sibling in the scratch tree. Existing input/version guards can pass because the original files and starting versions match; they do not bind the scratch plan's package roster to the final apply root. ApplyPermit authorizes a write but does not establish that it belongs to the planned workspace.

Controls: a normal prefix recovers correctly; missing trimmed sibling refuses E213; a sibling with a different starting version refuses E117. The incorrect success requires the colliding workspace/path/version conditions, not any workspace crash. Leading tabs also fail path recovery. This is a local data-integrity bug; no remote publishing scenario is claimed.

Correction direction: preserve native path bytes, removing only the protocol terminator, and verify exact checkpoint/scratch/apply workspace identity plus package roster before mutation. The regression should assert final package identity, version, note consumption and changelog, not only successful retry. Independent report: [recovery validation](validation-recovery/report.md).

**QA-02 — Native version data survives the bump but disappears from the requirement. CONFIRMED.**

A Python package at `2!0.4.8` patch-releases to `2!0.4.9`. Its co-released dependent's supported `>=2!0.4.8` declaration becomes `>=0.4.9`. The CLI exits0. Independent pip-packaging evaluation proves an epoch-zero version such as99.0.0 was rejected before and accepted after; the old dependency version remains accepted too. An epoch-zero control raises its floor correctly.

`render_target` reconstructs a stable target from major/minor/patch, omitting PEP440 epoch. Native bump arithmetic correctly retains the epoch. Checking only whether the new target satisfies the rewritten requirement is too weak: a wider, wrong range still contains that target.

The discovery matrix used seed180026,32 version/requirement cases, supported operators and optional extras/markers.26 commands succeeded;13 successful cases failed the semantic oracle. These are related manifestations, not13 independent bugs. Exact epoch pins also produced E319 rather than a valid rewrite in some cases. Runtime and optional-extra sites share the renderer; compatible-release and upper-bound renderers need the same sibling review. Poetry input is not claimed independently verified.

Correction direction: render using native PEP440 semantics, preserving epoch and intended precision. Assert both target inclusion and preservation of forbidden older versions. Independent current-binary evidence: [semantic/path validation](validation-semantics-paths/report.md), `current-binary-validation.json`; discovery/minimal repro: [semantic campaign](semantics/report.md).

**QA-03 — A filesystem identity is reinterpreted as a Git pattern. CONFIRMED.**

With packages under `packages/odd*` and `packages/odd-other`, a fix committed only to the sibling makes automatic inference patch-release both. Native `git log` using a literal pathspec returns no history for the untouched owner; the raw pathspec used by Callisto includes the sibling's commit. An own-only control bumps only the owner. An interior-star example did not reproduce the false positive, so this report identifies the proven terminal-star trigger precisely.

`commits_since` passes package directories directly after `--`. That terminates options but does not disable Git pathspec wildcard semantics. `first_parent_commits_touching` is a structurally related raw-path caller. Other change-listing code already has literal-path treatment, so the contract is inconsistent between sibling operations.

Correction direction: centralize literal package-path arguments at the Git boundary and migrate all callers whose inputs are filesystem identities. Test an untouched wildcard-named directory alongside a touched sibling, using native literal Git history as oracle. Evidence: [independent current-binary results](validation-semantics-paths/current-binary-validation.json).

**QA-04 — Message data collides with record framing. CONFIRMED.**

An otherwise ordinary `fix:` commit whose body contains U+001E causes `version --dry-run` to fail E026 while reading history. Ordinary-text and U+001F controls infer the expected patch. The current binary was independently tested; no alternate records or hostile messages were constructed.

Git accepts the body character. Callisto emits full message data inside a custom separator format and later splits on that same unescaped separator. The parser fails closed, so the demonstrated impact is blocked automatic inference, not incorrect publication or code execution. Severity is Low because the trigger is unusual.

Correction direction: use unambiguous record framing and preserve body content. Keep this boundary regression separate from tests that only feed malformed synthetic backend output. Source trace and controls are in [semantic/path validation](validation-semantics-paths/report.md).

**QA-05 — Native dependency context is lost during publication graph projection. CONFIRMED.**

For dual Cargo/npm owners A and B, a Cargo-only dependency A→B is attached not only to Cargo A's publication but also to npm A's publication. Independent reverse controls show an npm-only edge also ordering the unrelated Cargo output. Fresh fixtures with distinct native names reproduce both on the frozen current binary.

`link_publish_prerequisites` loops over every selected output, then every dependency of its owner. It filters the dependency destination by the declaring manifest's ecosystem, but never filters whether the selected dependent output belongs to that ecosystem. Accepted ADR12 and the current-behavior portion of the polyglot architecture require distribution-context publication edges. Shared tags correctly remain owner-level barriers; that does not authorize copying native prerequisites to all outputs.

Opposing native edges also expose a related ambiguity: independently acyclic Cargo/npm graphs can be rejected as an owner cycle. The current release spec explicitly rejects package-level runtime/build/optional cycles, so this cycle behavior is recorded as model/spec tension, not a second confirmed defect or a newly invented gate.

Correction direction: retain declaring distribution context when projecting native edges. Resolve owner-level cycle policy explicitly before changing it. Independent source/contract adjudication: [architecture report](validation-architecture/report.md), `current-fac8-results.json`.

**QA-06 — Equivalent historical queries are repeated for every tag. CONFIRMED.**

A repository originally contains a Cargo package, then replaces it with a same-named npm package. All old annotated version tags point to one old commit. Correct behavior rejects those tags as foreign. The defect is the cost: each different tag name misses historical caches even though its tree is identical, and selection starts over on a shrinking candidate list.

Independent command-count fixtures confirmed the pattern. Root expanded it on the current binary. One package, one historical source commit and unchanged working tree:

| Rejected historical tags | Git processes | Native median wall time |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
|1|10|176ms|
|10|64|622ms|
|50|304|2,993ms|

Process counts used a transparent logging wrapper; wall times were measured separately without that wrapper, three runs per cell. The wrapped runs are not used as production latency evidence. Raw records: `perf/foreign-measured/foreign-tag-results.json` and `native-wall-results.json`. Independent smaller controls: `validation-architecture/foreign-tags/results.json`.

The observed process formula is6T+4 for these fixtures. `Rosters` uses raw tag strings in `(rev,path)` and `(rev,name)` keys, so same-commit tags repeat identical historical probes. The rejection loop also reparses T+(T−1)+…+1 candidates. A constant process count on ordinary tag layouts does not cover this ownership-migration shape.

Correction direction: batch tag peeling, key immutable history caches by commit identity, and parse/order candidate versions once before checking ownership. Preserve version/tag-name tie-breaking and historical ownership rules. Parallelizing repeated queries would retain the underlying defect.

A separate explicit-shared-template path reparses identical candidates per package. It is a low-priority optimization, not a seventh primary defect: the whole-CLI measurement was619ms for500 packages sharing5000 tags, and does not isolate parser CPU. Cache semantic selection by exact template and grammar only for name-only selection; ownership-filtered paths need their own context. Detailed caveats: [performance adjudication](validation-architecture/performance-adjudication.md).

**How the swarm worked**

Three discovery agents partitioned failure modes across the workspace: semantic ordering/native requirements, boundary/parser behavior, and crash/retry recovery. Three separate validation roles reconstructed cases, tried negative controls and adjudicated contracts. Root owned builds, coverage-guided fuzzing, performance measurements, revision freezing and final classification. Six agents participated across the two waves; this was not six simultaneous Cargo builds. Cargo builds remained serialized.

The campaign used industry failure patterns as test strategies: native grammar differential oracles; graph closure and permutation invariants; valid awkward paths; delimiter/data separation; interruption after acknowledgment but before subsequent writes; stale/wrong-context evidence; and immutable-identity cache keys. These patterns generated candidates, not conclusions. Every confirmed finding has a concrete source-to-observable-outcome trace and a sibling sweep.

Three agent turns stopped with tool-side content-filter errors. Their saved evidence was not accepted blindly: successful independent roles and root reconstructed the benign regression cases. No additional exploitation work was pursued. A21-row broad fault-injection harness had a SyntaxError in its shim; all21 rows are excluded from product test coverage. The valid checkpoint scenarios were separately rebuilt and executed. An initial Python-oracle harness parsing error is likewise excluded; the corrected32-case campaign is the one counted.

**Fuzzing and executed evidence**

| Campaign | Executed result | Oracle / scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest editor libFuzzer |90,613 inputs, exit0|Open or clean error; successful write must parse/read back its target|
| Manifest identity libFuzzer |213,660 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
| Changeset parser libFuzzer |467,578 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
| Package-id parser libFuzzer |565,938 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
| Python semantic generator |32 cases, seed180026|Independent pip-packaging requirement/version semantics|
| Graph/permutation generator |48 discovery-revision dry runs, seed181126; no mismatches|Independent monotone closure oracle over24 six-node DAGs, each permuted|
| Boundary campaigns |Depth, pathspec and8 message-body character controls|Current contract plus native Git literal/history behavior|
| Recovery validation |Four independent original fixtures plus fresh current-binary crash/retry replay|Manifest identity/version, notes, changelog and sibling state|
| Native publication graph |Three independent fixtures, repeated on current binary|Accepted distribution-level ordering contract|
| Performance |Same-commit foreign-tag counts and separate native timings|Identical history/tree state, varying tag aliases|

The48 graph/permutation controls ran on the initial discovery binary; the newer revision changes peer policy, so those passing controls are not represented as current-revision validation. The reported defects were separately reproduced on the current binary.

Total coverage-guided inputs: **1,337,789**, with no crash observed. These are bounded smoke campaigns, not an assurance of crash freedom. Seed181126, maximum configured input8192 bytes, bounded per-input time and memory were recorded in the commands/logs. The manifest editor ran30 seconds; the other targets12 seconds each (libFuzzer reported31/13-second elapsed totals).

The original macOS fuzz build first hit a restricted shared-cache download, then a sanitizer-coverage link failure from `pep440_rs`'s auxiliary cdylib target. The successful isolated harness used offline cached dependencies and a temporary copy of the same dependency source with only the unused cdylib build target removed. No algorithm source changed. Sanitizer mode was `none`; coverage feedback and debug/overflow assertions were enabled. Do not describe this as an ASan run. Fuzz sources point to the frozen current Callisto source. Logs, corpus, command metadata and adaptation are retained in `fuzz/`, `corpus/` and `fuzz-summary.json`.

This explains why semantic fuzzing mattered: a crash fuzzer can pass while a successful command weakens a constraint, selects the wrong directory or applies the wrong plan. Stronger state/content oracles found the important defects.

**Patterns and architectural implications**

| Pattern | Findings | Missing enforcement | Appropriate existing responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lossy Git boundary conversions |QA-01,03,04|Filesystem identity and message data must survive Git protocol transformations|GitVcsProvider / current GitAccess boundary|
| Native context dropped during projection |QA-02,05|Epoch and declaring distribution must survive generic planning/rendering|VersionSpecRenderer and distribution-level graph projection|
| Plan authority weaker than mutation authority |QA-01|A plan must belong to the workspace/package roster it mutates|Version apply/checkpoint preparation; ApplyPermit alone is insufficient|
| Cache identity differs from semantic identity |QA-06|Equivalent immutable revisions should share observation work|Historical identity resolver and Git query cache|

The existing native models already hold much of the lost information. The first corrections should be local, explicit operations and constructors that preserve it. This does not justify introducing seven new traits, replacing the synchronous runner, adding Tokio, or creating a second release workflow framework. The skill's seven responsibility names are useful ownership categories: PackageIdentityResolver, VersionSpecRenderer, ChangesetStorage, CstManifestEditor, GitVcsProvider, CascadeSolver and ReportPresenter. No new CST-fidelity or report-format defect was established in this campaign merely to fill those categories.

Recovery needs an explicit workspace/plan binding; requirement validation needs a monotonic floor oracle in addition to target inclusion; publication projection needs a contextual edge query. These are semantic contracts worth enforcing by types/private constructors where possible. The related defect families are marked for architectural review before remediation. No remediation or spec change was performed here.

**Prior findings, exclusions and limits**

The ten findings in the17 November report are historical results at `ab3c030`, not ten additional current open bugs. While this campaign ran, external merges changed many of those areas. I did not perform a complete post-remediation verification of all ten and therefore do not label them all fixed or all still open. The new six were revalidated on `fac8cad` and are the current confirmed list from this campaign.

Depth32 discovery is an explicit contract, so deeper-package omission was refuted as a new bug. The owner-cycle ambiguity is a design/spec reconciliation item. Shared-template parsing is an optimization follow-up. Known older ledger findings were excluded from new discovery.

No live registry mutation, real forge write or full hosted workflow was exercised. Full `just ci`, current full-suite coverage, a mutation-testing campaign and all grammars/platforms were not run. This campaign uses generated tests and the existing real CLI, not comprehensive proof. Entire Brain context retrieval failed its external lock, so direct source supplied the relevant query's evidence. No automatic approval-review rejection blocked the work; the agent content-filter interruptions are recorded separately above.

Recommended remediation order: QA-01 first, then QA-02/03, then QA-05, QA-06 and QA-04. Add boundary-level regressions with negative controls, migrate all affected sibling call sites, and run the repository's required checks on resulting changes. This report itself is not a PR readiness verdict.

Machine-readable evidence: [finding-report.json](finding-report.json), [workspace-manifest.json](workspace-manifest.json), candidate/assessment and field-survival directories. Independent reports are under `validation-recovery/`, `validation-semantics-paths/` and `validation-architecture/`; original semantic campaign is under `semantics/`.

|1|10|176ms|
|10|64|622ms|
|50|304|2,993ms|

Process counts used a transparent logging wrapper; wall times were measured separately without that wrapper, three runs per cell. The wrapped runs are not used as production latency evidence. Raw records: `perf/foreign-measured/foreign-tag-results.json` and `native-wall-results.json`. Independent smaller controls: `validation-architecture/foreign-tags/results.json`.

The observed process formula is6T+4 for these fixtures. `Rosters` uses raw tag strings in `(rev,path)` and `(rev,name)` keys, so same-commit tags repeat identical historical probes. The rejection loop also reparses T+(T−1)+…+1 candidates. A constant process count on ordinary tag layouts does not cover this ownership-migration shape.

Correction direction: batch tag peeling, key immutable history caches by commit identity, and parse/order candidate versions once before checking ownership. Preserve version/tag-name tie-breaking and historical ownership rules. Parallelizing repeated queries would retain the underlying defect.

A separate explicit-shared-template path reparses identical candidates per package. It is a low-priority optimization, not a seventh primary defect: the whole-CLI measurement was619ms for500 packages sharing5000 tags, and does not isolate parser CPU. Cache semantic selection by exact template and grammar only for name-only selection; ownership-filtered paths need their own context. Detailed caveats: [performance adjudication](validation-architecture/performance-adjudication.md).

**How the swarm worked**

Three discovery agents partitioned failure modes across the workspace: semantic ordering/native requirements, boundary/parser behavior, and crash/retry recovery. Three separate validation roles reconstructed cases, tried negative controls and adjudicated contracts. Root owned builds, coverage-guided fuzzing, performance measurements, revision freezing and final classification. Six agents participated across the two waves; this was not six simultaneous Cargo builds. Cargo builds remained serialized.

The campaign used industry failure patterns as test strategies: native grammar differential oracles; graph closure and permutation invariants; valid awkward paths; delimiter/data separation; interruption after acknowledgment but before subsequent writes; stale/wrong-context evidence; and immutable-identity cache keys. These patterns generated candidates, not conclusions. Every confirmed finding has a concrete source-to-observable-outcome trace and a sibling sweep.

Three agent turns stopped with tool-side content-filter errors. Their saved evidence was not accepted blindly: successful independent roles and root reconstructed the benign regression cases. No additional exploitation work was pursued. A21-row broad fault-injection harness had a SyntaxError in its shim; all21 rows are excluded from product test coverage. The valid checkpoint scenarios were separately rebuilt and executed. An initial Python-oracle harness parsing error is likewise excluded; the corrected32-case campaign is the one counted.

**Fuzzing and executed evidence**

| Campaign | Executed result | Oracle / scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest editor libFuzzer |90,613 inputs, exit0|Open or clean error; successful write must parse/read back its target|
| Manifest identity libFuzzer |213,660 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
| Changeset parser libFuzzer |467,578 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
| Package-id parser libFuzzer |565,938 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
| Python semantic generator |32 cases, seed180026|Independent pip-packaging requirement/version semantics|
| Graph/permutation generator |48 discovery-revision dry runs, seed181126; no mismatches|Independent monotone closure oracle over24 six-node DAGs, each permuted|
| Boundary campaigns |Depth, pathspec and8 message-body character controls|Current contract plus native Git literal/history behavior|
| Recovery validation |Four independent original fixtures plus fresh current-binary crash/retry replay|Manifest identity/version, notes, changelog and sibling state|
| Native publication graph |Three independent fixtures, repeated on current binary|Accepted distribution-level ordering contract|
| Performance |Same-commit foreign-tag counts and separate native timings|Identical history/tree state, varying tag aliases|

The48 graph/permutation controls ran on the initial discovery binary; the newer revision changes peer policy, so those passing controls are not represented as current-revision validation. The reported defects were separately reproduced on the current binary.

Total coverage-guided inputs: **1,337,789**, with no crash observed. These are bounded smoke campaigns, not an assurance of crash freedom. Seed181126, maximum configured input8192 bytes, bounded per-input time and memory were recorded in the commands/logs. The manifest editor ran30 seconds; the other targets12 seconds each (libFuzzer reported31/13-second elapsed totals).

The original macOS fuzz build first hit a restricted shared-cache download, then a sanitizer-coverage link failure from `pep440_rs`'s auxiliary cdylib target. The successful isolated harness used offline cached dependencies and a temporary copy of the same dependency source with only the unused cdylib build target removed. No algorithm source changed. Sanitizer mode was `none`; coverage feedback and debug/overflow assertions were enabled. Do not describe this as an ASan run. Fuzz sources point to the frozen current Callisto source. Logs, corpus, command metadata and adaptation are retained in `fuzz/`, `corpus/` and `fuzz-summary.json`.

This explains why semantic fuzzing mattered: a crash fuzzer can pass while a successful command weakens a constraint, selects the wrong directory or applies the wrong plan. Stronger state/content oracles found the important defects.

**Patterns and architectural implications**

| Pattern | Findings | Missing enforcement | Appropriate existing responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lossy Git boundary conversions |QA-01,03,04|Filesystem identity and message data must survive Git protocol transformations|GitVcsProvider / current GitAccess boundary|
| Native context dropped during projection |QA-02,05|Epoch and declaring distribution must survive generic planning/rendering|VersionSpecRenderer and distribution-level graph projection|
| Plan authority weaker than mutation authority |QA-01|A plan must belong to the workspace/package roster it mutates|Version apply/checkpoint preparation; ApplyPermit alone is insufficient|
| Cache identity differs from semantic identity |QA-06|Equivalent immutable revisions should share observation work|Historical identity resolver and Git query cache|

The existing native models already hold much of the lost information. The first corrections should be local, explicit operations and constructors that preserve it. This does not justify introducing seven new traits, replacing the synchronous runner, adding Tokio, or creating a second release workflow framework. The skill's seven responsibility names are useful ownership categories: PackageIdentityResolver, VersionSpecRenderer, ChangesetStorage, CstManifestEditor, GitVcsProvider, CascadeSolver and ReportPresenter. No new CST-fidelity or report-format defect was established in this campaign merely to fill those categories.

Recovery needs an explicit workspace/plan binding; requirement validation needs a monotonic floor oracle in addition to target inclusion; publication projection needs a contextual edge query. These are semantic contracts worth enforcing by types/private constructors where possible. The related defect families are marked for architectural review before remediation. No remediation or spec change was performed here.

**Prior findings, exclusions and limits**

The ten findings in the17 November report are historical results at `ab3c030`, not ten additional current open bugs. While this campaign ran, external merges changed many of those areas. I did not perform a complete post-remediation verification of all ten and therefore do not label them all fixed or all still open. The new six were revalidated on `fac8cad` and are the current confirmed list from this campaign.

Depth32 discovery is an explicit contract, so deeper-package omission was refuted as a new bug. The owner-cycle ambiguity is a design/spec reconciliation item. Shared-template parsing is an optimization follow-up. Known older ledger findings were excluded from new discovery.

No live registry mutation, real forge write or full hosted workflow was exercised. Full `just ci`, current full-suite coverage, a mutation-testing campaign and all grammars/platforms were not run. This campaign uses generated tests and the existing real CLI, not comprehensive proof. Entire Brain context retrieval failed its external lock, so direct source supplied the relevant query's evidence. No automatic approval-review rejection blocked the work; the agent content-filter interruptions are recorded separately above.

Recommended remediation order: QA-01 first, then QA-02/03, then QA-05, QA-06 and QA-04. Add boundary-level regressions with negative controls, migrate all affected sibling call sites, and run the repository's required checks on resulting changes. This report itself is not a PR readiness verdict.

Machine-readable evidence: [finding-report.json](finding-report.json), [workspace-manifest.json](workspace-manifest.json), candidate/assessment and field-survival directories. Independent reports are under `validation-recovery/`, `validation-semantics-paths/` and `validation-architecture/`; original semantic campaign is under `semantics/`.

---
callisto-cli: patch
---

**Large pnpm workspaces load much faster.** Relative `workspace:../path` dependencies are now resolved through one directory index instead of a scan per dependency.

- At 800 packages with relative `workspace:` paths, `status` drops from about 4.9 s to 0.6 s, `version --dry-run` from 7.6 s to 0.8 s and `release --dry-run` from 6.3 s to 0.9 s.
- No configuration change is needed. Dependency edges and warnings are unchanged.
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

**`release-pr` JSON arguments report where a failure came from.** A relative `--decision` or `--snapshot` file is now read relative to `--cwd`, and a bad file no longer looks like a usage mistake.

- Malformed inline or stdin JSON is still `E281`, exit 2, naming the flag.
- A malformed file is `E238`, exit 1, naming the file; an unreadable file is `E213`.
- `compose-pr-body --preview` follows the same rule: a malformed preview file is `E238`, exit 1, instead of `E281`.
- **Scripting:** treat exit 1 from a file argument as a data problem, not a bad invocation.
---
callisto-cli: minor
---

**Release PRs open for releases inferred from commits.** A package with `release-trigger = "auto"` now gets a release PR from its commits alone; it no longer needs a changeset to be released.

- `release-pr decide` opens a PR whenever `callisto version` would version a package, after groups and dependents.
- A changeset that cannot be parsed now fails `release-pr decide` with the error `version` reports, instead of a green run that releases nothing.
- `status` no longer warns `inferred-release-without-changeset`; that diagnostic code is gone.

**Scripting:** `version --emit-decision` writes decision schema 3, which adds `consumedChangesets`. Release verification (E165) checks that the release commit deletes exactly those changesets. Schema 1 and 2 decisions still read.

input.content:
fix(vcs): keep native path and message bytes across the Git boundary

A workspace prefix lost its leading spaces, so an interrupted version run could resume a similarly named sibling. Package directories were passed to Git as raw pathspecs, so `packages/odd*` matched `packages/odd-other`'s history and its files when staging the version commit. Commit messages were framed with U+001E, which a message body may contain.

- Path output from Git strips only its terminating newline (`CommandOutput::stdout_line`).
- `literal_pathspec` is the one constructor for filesystem-identity pathspecs: commit inference, first-parent history, `commit_adding`, version-commit staging and changeset PR lookup use it.
- `commits_since` reads `git log -z`, NUL-framed.

     - The parser runs `record.trim_end_matches('\n')` before `split_once('\n')`, so the record becomes `"<sha>"`, the split fails, and it returns `MalformedLogOutput` (E301).
     - The old code got `"<sha>\x1f"` and parsed it fine with an empty summary.
     - Failure scenario: one empty-message commit anywhere in a package's history makes every `commits_since` over it fail. FullHistory inference for an untagged package hits this permanently, so `version`/`status` stop working on that repo. Converted repos and some bots produce such commits.

     - `git show` of the decision JSON keeps any trailing whitespace or `\r`, and serde_json accepts it.
     - The `for-each-ref` tags digest is unchanged, because that output has no leading whitespace, so in-flight checkpoints stay compatible.
     - Only a runner that emits `\r\n` would now break `CommitSha::parse`. That needs a wrapper that rewrites git's output, so it is not reachable with real git.

#!/bin/sh
# Usage: mutants.sh <name> <base> <crate>...
name=$1; base=$2; shift 2
out="$TMPDIR/mut-$name"
mkdir -p "$out"
/usr/bin/git diff "$base" -- 'crates/*/src' > "$out/diff"
pkgs=""
for c in "$@"; do pkgs="$pkgs -p $c"; done
export CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0
export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(( $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) / 5 ))
cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff "$out/diff" $pkgs --output "$out" > "$out/log" 2>&1
code=$?
echo "mutants exit $code" >> "$out/log"
echo "$out"
exit $code

Fixes QA-01 (trigger), QA-03 and QA-04 from the 2026-11-18 QA swarm: Git output and pathspecs now carry a path's and a message's own bytes.

**What changed**

- Path output from Git strips only its terminating newline (`CommandOutput::stdout_line`): `--show-prefix`, `--show-toplevel`, `--absolute-git-dir`, `--git-path` and the release-commit check. A workspace named `  release-work` no longer resumes its sibling `release-work`.
- `vcs::literal_pathspec` is the one constructor for filesystem-identity pathspecs. Used by `commits_since`, `first_parent_commits_touching`, `first_parent_commits_by_path`, `commit_adding`, version-commit staging (`git add`/`git rm --cached`) and changeset PR lookup.
- `commits_since` reads `git log -z --format=%H%n%B`. A body with U+001E/U+001F/U+0001 is read, and an empty message is a commit, not E301.
- Checkpoint listings (`files_at`, `files_named`) and release-commit verification (`diff-tree --name-status`) read `-z` output, so a name with non-ASCII, `"`, `\` or a tab is not Git's quoted form.

**Tests (real git)**

- `a_directory_named_with_a_glob_selects_only_its_own_history`, `staging_a_written_path_named_with_a_glob_stages_only_that_path`, `commits_since_keeps_a_body_holding_framing_characters`, `commits_since_reads_a_commit_with_an_empty_message`, `a_workspace_prefix_keeps_its_leading_and_trailing_spaces`, `checkpoint_listings_name_files_by_their_own_bytes`.
- End to end: `a_workspace_named_with_leading_spaces_resumes_itself_not_its_sibling` interrupts `version` in `  release-work` next to `release-work` (same crates and versions, different changeset) and asserts the resumed repository equals an uninterrupted run: package identity, version, consumed notes and changelog in both directories. It fails with the checkpoint trim restored.

**Sibling sweep**

- Fixed here: version-commit staging (a `p/odd*/a` write also staged `p/odd-other/a`), `changeset_prs` pathspec, release-commit `--show-prefix` and `diff-tree` quoting, checkpoint listings.
- Unchanged, checked: `check-ignore` takes paths literally (rejects pathspec magic); `ls-tree` paths are literal; `is_staged` already uses `--literal-pathspecs`; `files_containing_at` takes intended `:(glob)` specs.
- Deferred: `changeset_prs` frames commit subjects with U+0001 and reads `--name-only` without `-z`. A subject containing U+0001 or a non-ASCII changeset file name drops that changeset's PR link from the changelog. Impact is a missing link only; `-z` with `--name-only` has no unambiguous subject/name boundary, so it needs its own format.

**Checks**

- `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`: exit 0.
- `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` on the Rust diff (model, graph): 0 missed.

Recovery plan binding (QA-01's second half) follows in WP T.

23:A crash or a failed lockfile refresh can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same plan again is file-level idempotent, and a fresh run recovers that plan from a checkpoint ([ADR 13](../adr/0013-interrupted-version-runs-resume-from-a-checkpoint-ref.md)):
25:- Before its first write, `version` records `HEAD`, the index and the workspace's working tree (untracked files included) as a commit at `refs/worktree/callisto/checkpoint/version`, with `HEAD`, a digest of the tags and the Callisto version in its message (`GitAccess::create_checkpoint`, through `CommandRunner::run_with_env` and a temporary index). It is created only if absent (E341), never signed, and deleted after the last effect, including the emitted decision and preview.
26:- A run that finds the checkpoint checks it out in a temporary worktree (with `HEAD` on the commit the run started from, so commit inference reads real history), loads the workspace there and plans as usual with the date the interrupted run used. `resume_input_changes` then applies that plan in the worktree, without a lockfile refresh, to get the tree a finished run leaves. Every file the plan was derived from (the manifests the loader opened, `callisto.toml`, the changesets) and every file it writes must be on disk either as the checkpoint recorded it or as that expected tree has it, compared through Git's filters, and a file the expected tree lacks counts as the run's deletion only when the index lacks it too; `HEAD`, the tags, the Callisto version and the workspace must match. Anything else refuses with E340, whose help names the way out: delete the checkpoint ref and follow the E121 steps. Only then is the plan applied to the real tree. A dry run has no permit to apply in the worktree, so it reports the plan without this check. The apply's preflight and workspace resolution run before the checkpoint is created (`apply::validate_plan`), so a run that cannot start leaves no checkpoint, and a plan that writes nothing records none. The checkpoint's temporary index starts from a copy of the real one and adds the working tree tolerating unreadable files; the scratch checkout runs none of the user's hooks.
27:- E121 still guards states no checkpoint recorded.
31:- Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. With no checkpoint (a state another tool or an older Callisto left), E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified.
39:Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` or `--emit-preview` write failure leaves the checkpoint in place, so running `version` again writes them.
296:      "criterion": "Outside `mode: pre` and when no checkpoint exists (VER-APPLY-18), after planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk effective version differs from its version at `HEAD`, or when its effective version staged in the git index differs from `HEAD`, provided a changeset remains in the `HEAD` tree or configured working-tree changesets directory (including untracked files), or a canonical manifest is staged. - Before its first write, `version` records `HEAD`, the index and the workspace's working tree (untracked files included) as a commit at `refs/worktree/callisto/checkpoint/version`, with `HEAD`, a digest of the tags and the Callisto version in its message (`GitAccess::create_checkpoint`, through `CommandRunner::run_with_env` and a temporary index). It is created only if absent (E341), never signed, and deleted after the last effect, including the emitted decision and preview.

-- A run that finds the checkpoint checks it out in a temporary worktree (with `HEAD` on the commit the run started from, so commit inference reads real history), loads the workspace there and plans as usual with the date the interrupted run used. `resume_input_changes` then applies that plan in the worktree, without a lockfile refresh, to get the tree a finished run leaves. Every file the plan was derived from (the manifests the loader opened, `callisto.toml`, the changesets) and every file it writes must be on disk either as the checkpoint recorded it or as that expected tree has it, compared through Git's filters, and a file the expected tree lacks counts as the run's deletion only when the index lacks it too; `HEAD`, the tags, the Callisto version and the workspace must match, and the temporary worktree directory the plan came from must hold this workspace's tree in the checkpoint, so a plan made in another directory is never applied. Closes QA-01's plan-binding half and GAP-04 from the 2026-11-18 QA swarm. The path-identity fix that makes the QA-01 retry resume correctly is #577 (WP S); this PR makes a wrong plan unappliable even if a path is lost again.

**What changed**

- `resume_input_changes` refuses (E340) unless the scratch directory the plan came from holds this workspace's tree in the checkpoint (`<checkpoint>:./` from both roots), and returns at once so no scratch error masks it. Two `rev-parse` per side, once per resume. No new types or permits.
- GAP-04: a finished run leaves its `--emit-decision`/`--emit-preview` files, so the CLI writes them into the scratch tree before the existing comparison. An identical retry after a run that emitted into `.changeset` and was interrupted no longer refuses itself with E340; a hand edit to that file is still refused.
- The fixture `GitRunner` passes a child environment, so graph tests drive the real checkpoint path.
- `docs/architecture/versioning.md` and `docs/specs/versioning.json` describe both.

**Tests**

- `a_resume_refuses_a_plan_made_in_a_sibling_directory_of_the_checkpoint` (graph, real git): real checkpoint and scratch worktree, sibling with the same package and version and a different changeset. Without the check every input comparison passes and the result is empty; the primary directory resumes with no changes.
- `a_decision_emitted_into_the_changesets_directory_does_not_block_the_resume` (CLI): decision into `.changeset/decision.json`, preview write fails, retry. Unedited: succeeds, decision unchanged, preview written, checkpoint gone. Edited: E340 naming `decision.json`. The unedited case failed with E340 before the fix.

**Review**

Fresh Opus review found no blockers. Applied: early return on a tree mismatch. Not changed, low:

- A dry run with a checkpoint skips the resume check (no permit), so it can report another directory's plan. It writes nothing.
- A byte-identical sibling passes the tree check. Inferred commits are path-scoped, so they could differ, but this needs the path loss fixed in #577 to recur.
- A workspace root chosen by a marker absent from the checkpoint (an ignored-only `.moon/`) now refuses rather than planning elsewhere.

**Checks**

- `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`: exit 0.
- `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` (graph, cli): 16 tested, 12 caught, 4 unviable, 0 missed.

1:# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership
13:- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
14:- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
15:- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
19:- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
29:- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.

docs/architecture/identity.md:51:For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `history::sole_owner_at` picks the same-named candidate whose first canonical manifest path held a manifest declaring the name at the tag's commit. When none does, because the directory moved or the package gained a higher-priority manifest, it asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name at that commit, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, taken from the identity index. Two or more matches, or none, mean no owner. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies the same check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner. A bare key that matches one current package is checked too: if `pre.json` was added when a manifest of another ecosystem held the name and the package had none, the key pins nothing.
docs/architecture/release.md:13:- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish. The operations form a DAG by prerequisite; `callisto_model::canonical_operation_order`, built on `michi-graph`, validates it (a cycle is reported as one operation on it) and fixes the order: the smallest topological order by operation id.
docs/architecture/release.md:118:The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. Selecting one identity of a dual package releases every identity of that package, so the tag never waits on a subset of its publishes. A product's public release also waits for the tag, and so the registry publishes, of each other package whose asset it carries. An intent derived before either rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.
